Q: How do I display a local image in Markdown? A:

To add an image in a Markdown file, the .md file and the image should be in the same directory. As in my case, my .md file was in the doc folder, so I also moved the image into the same folder.

After that, write the following syntax in the .md file:

![alt text](filename)

Like ![Car Image](car.png).

This has worked for me.

Q: Is there a way to ignore header lines in a UNIX sort? A:

If the only lines preceded with : are in the header, and the colon does not appear anywhere else, it is possible to sort it with sort alone with the command

your_command | sort -t ':' -k1,1 -s

How it works

  1. -t ':' defined the colon as a field separator.
  2. -k1,1 tells to sort using only the value of the first field.
  3. -s makes the sorting stable.

This way, all lines starting with : will have an empty first field. All other lines will be sorted by their values.

Example

$ cat file | sort -s -t ':' -k1,1
:0:12345
:2:4:8
:2:3:4
:1:6:2:3:3:8:4:2
:0:0:0
010005TSTDOG_FOOD01
222334NOTALINEOUT01
325611LVEANOTHERS00
477821USASHUTTLES21
500123TSTMY_RADAR00

Caveats

Again, there are prerequisites:

  1. Lines starting with : should only appear on the header.
  2. : should never appear in any other line.

If the first condition is not met, all "commented" lines will bubble up to the header.

If the second condition is not met, lines with colon will have the rest of it ignored. For example, if we have a file like this one:

:9900
:1100
:0099
00:99
11_99
00:11
11_11
00:00
11_00

...lines with the colon will only be sorted by the values before it:

$ cat file2 | sort -s -t ':' -k1,1
:9900
:1100
:0099
00:99
00:11
00:00
11_00
11_11
11_99

Q: How can I use a variable from iframe to another iframe in a different domain? A:

The frames can't communicate directly but you can communicate via a server you control. This server can be on any domain.

You can push events using AJAX and receive events using server-sent-events. Make sure you're dealing with the cross domain requests appropriately by implementing CORS on the server.

Q: In what file are __io_putchar() and __io_getchar() defined? A:

This one took me a second to figure out as well, but take a look around the generated code and you'll see a macro definition like this:

#elif defined(__GNUC__)
#define PUTCHAR_PROTOTYPE int __io_putchar(int ch)
#endif /* __ICCARM__ */

(here I'm using the gcc toolcahin).

Then look for where that macro is used. In my project, it looked something like this (might differ if you're not using UART):

/**
  * @brief  Retargets the C library printf function to the USART.
  */
PUTCHAR_PROTOTYPE
{
  (void)HAL_UART_Transmit(&hcom_uart [COM_ActiveLogPort], (uint8_t *) &ch, 1, COM_POLL_TIMEOUT);
  return ch;
}

The definition is being masked by the macro, which is why you won't find it with a find-all.

(Note, I was using a board configuration, which I think is what you'd have if you selected the discovery kit for your MCU. For an MCU-only configuration, you would have to then implement this yourself, as Ján's answer suggests).

Q: Problem with DWT3D with Custom Keras Layer A:

It failed because there's a conflict between Keras, which automatically inferences shapes, and how TFDWT creates tensors.

When you compile the model, Keras tries to determine the shapes of the tensors in the network, so it traces the layer with a scratch graph. It calls self.dwt3d(x), which triggers dwt3d.build(), which then creates the tensor in that graph. When Keras finishes determining the shapes, it deletes this scratch graph. When the training starts, your DWT3D layer tries to use that matrix, but it can't because it belongs to a graph that was deleted.

Your solution will work, but here is a cleaner way to do it:

class DWTLayer(keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.dwt3d = DWT3D(wave='haar')

    def build(self, input_shape):
        with tf.init_scope():
            self.dwt3d.build(input_shape)
        super().build(input_shape)
    
    def call(self, x):
        return self.dwt3d(x)
